Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Q4 pilot looks like a great fit. Procurement here asked me to send our standard PO template so we can start the onboarding flow. Attached is Clearline_PO_Template_v2.pdf. A couple of asks from AP before we can accept a PO: 

- Net terms: our standard is Net45, but we can consider Net60 for larger pilots. Can you confirm Redwood's preferred term for pilots?
- Invoice cadence: our AP team prefers weekly invoices for pilots (they reconcile weekly runs). Is Redwood able to support weekly invoices vs monthly?
- PO metadata: we need the following fields populated on the PO to match our ERP — Billing Entity (legal name), BU/Cost Center, GL code, and a 10-digit PO ID.
- Discounts/packaging: Can you confirm whether the Q4 pilot rate band (volume-based discount) requires consolidated monthly billing to qualify, or if we can keep weekly invoices and still get the same discount?

If you can review the template and send back a short note with any technical/ops constraints, I can loop in our AP lead to speed approvals.

Attachment: Clearline_PO_Template_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,

Subject: RE: PO metadata alignment + split-invoice cadence for Q4 pilot

Hi Alyssa — really appreciate the clear checklist and the template. Quick answers below and a proposed path forward.

Net terms: Redwood can accept Net45 for the pilot. For larger commitments we often move to Net60 depending on enterprise terms, but Net45 is fine to get started. We can also offer a 2% early-pay discount if Clearline can support a Net30 early-pay run (optional).

Invoice cadence: Technically we support both weekly and monthly invoice rails. One operational note: our standard volume-discount calculation is evaluated on a per-billing-period basis. Practically that means:
- Weekly invoices: discounts apply per weekly invoice (smaller aggregation).
- Consolidated monthly statement: allows us to aggregate usage across the month and apply the higher tiered discount bands.

Discount implication: if you need the full consolidated-month discount band for the pilot, we recommend weekly invoices + a consolidated monthly statement that rolls up the weekly lines for discounting purposes. That keeps AP happy with weekly remits but lets us compute the discount on monthly volumes.

PO metadata: we need the Billing Entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.), a clear GL mapping for each invoice line, and the 10-digit PO ID as you noted. If Clearline can include a Cost Center value we can map at invoice time to your ERP.

I've attached a short pricing/discount breakdown for the pilot that shows the two paths (weekly-only vs weekly + consolidated monthly rollup). See redwood-pricing-discount-breakdown.xlsx.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Alyssa — you confirm AP will accept weekly invoices with a consolidated monthly statement.
2) We exchange a one-page mutual action plan (I'll draft) that lists PO fields, billing contacts, and the minimum usage threshold for the highest discount tier.
3) You send the PO populated with the Redwood Billing Entity and PO ID; we trigger provisioning.

Looping Vanessa (AM) for the implementation cadence and Tessa (Finance ops) for the invoice mapping details.

Attachment: redwood-pricing-discount-breakdown.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Best,
Ben Carter

Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and the spreadsheet. A few clarifications from AP after an initial read: 

- Weekly invoices are preferable and non-negotiable for our pilot runs (cashflow control).
- Consolidated monthly statement is acceptable on our side, provided each weekly invoice contains the PO ID, GL code, and Cost Center so our system can auto-apply payments against the correct buckets.
- We cannot commit to an early-pay program (Net30) at this time. The Net45 term is standard for us.
- Discount ask: Clearline is asking if the 12% top-band discount can be honored if we do weekly invoices + consolidated monthly statement (we will meet the usage thresholds). If Redwood requires consolidated monthly invoicing (single invoice) to grant that band, that would be a blocker for us.

If you can send a one-page mutual action plan and the minimal PO example with the Redwood Billing Entity pre-filled, procurement can turn the PO around within 3 business days. 

Thanks,
Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — Vanessa here (Account Director). Thanks for outlining Clearline's AP constraints — totally understood. We run pilots like this often and the hybrid approach Ben suggested is what typically works: weekly invoice files that contain full PO and GL metadata, plus a consolidated monthly statement that aggregates the weekly lines for discount reconciliation.

Operational commitments from Redwood:
- We will include PO ID, GL code, and Cost Center on each weekly invoice line.
- We will generate a consolidated monthly statement (PDF + CSV) that shows aggregated usage and the applied discount for reconciliation purposes.
- To qualify for the top-tier 12% discount, we require a minimum commit of 120,000 inference units for the pilot month (this is reflected in the attached mutual action plan). If you meet that threshold across the month, we will apply the 12% on the consolidated statement retroactively and issue a credit or adjustment as needed.

I attached a short mutual-action-plan (redwood-q4-m-a-p.docx) that lists the PO fields, billing contacts, and milestone for the discount. If Clearline can add the Billing Entity (Redwood Inference, Inc.), a 10-digit PO, and confirm the Cost Center mapping, I can sign off and Ben can provision.
